# Wiring a Code App to a Connector (non-Dataverse) data source

Everything in [dataverse-web-api.md](dataverse-web-api.md) and [code-app-deployment.md](code-app-deployment.md) assumes a Dataverse-table data source. Wiring a Code App to a **Connector**-type data source instead — e.g. calling an existing Copilot Studio agent, SharePoint, or any other standard/premium connector — follows a different path with its own failure modes.

## 1. A connection must exist before you add the data source

Unlike Dataverse tables, a Connector-type data source needs a **Power Platform connection** (the OAuth-authenticated instance of a connector) to already exist. For any connector using interactive OAuth (Copilot Studio, most first-party connectors), that connection **cannot be created via API or CLI** — it must be created once, interactively, in the Maker Portal (make.powerapps.com → Connections → New connection).

Once the connection exists, add the data source:

```bash
pac code add-data-source --apiId <shortApiId> --connectionId <connection-guid> --environment <environment-url>
```

or, with the npm CLI (when it's usable — see the SDK/CLI split gotcha in [code-app-deployment.md](code-app-deployment.md)):

```bash
node node_modules/@microsoft/power-apps-cli/dist/Bin.js add-data-source -a <shortApiId> -c <connection-id>
```

**Gotcha — Git Bash / MSYS path mangling.** Any CLI argument starting with `/` gets silently rewritten into a Windows path by Git Bash's MSYS layer — `/providers/Microsoft.PowerApps/apis/shared_microsoftcopilotstudio` becomes something like `C:/Program Files/Git/providers/...`, and the call 404s. Fix: pass the **short** `apiId` (e.g. `shared_microsoftcopilotstudio`) instead of the full `/providers/...` path — it sidesteps the leading-slash rewrite entirely. (`MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` only partially helps and can leave a different double-slash artifact; the short-id form is simpler and sufficient.)

Successful `add-data-source` generates `src/generated/models/<Connector>Model.ts`, `src/generated/services/<Connector>Service.ts`, and updates `.power/schemas/appschemas/dataSourcesInfo.ts` with a `dataSourceType: "Connector"` entry (full API path templates, e.g. `.../proactivecopilot/executeAsyncV2`). It also adds a `connectionReferences` entry to `power.config.json`.

## 2. The client-side singleton race (`"Data source not found: <connectorKey>"`)

**Symptom:** `add-data-source` succeeds, the connection is healthy (Maker Portal connection **Details** page shows "Status: Connected" and lists your app under "Apps using this connection"), the generated service/model files look correct — but calling any operation on the generated `<Connector>Service` throws at runtime:

```
Data source not found: <connectorKey>
```

**Root cause — not a server-side provisioning gap.** Apps scaffolded by tools like vibe.powerapps.com carry **two independent, parallel Dataverse client layers**:

1. `app-gen-sdk/data/...` (`AppGenByocDataClient`) — used by every pre-existing generated hook (`src/generated/hooks/*.ts` → `src/generated/services/*-service.ts`). Its `getDataSourcesInfo()` (in `app-gen-sdk/data/common/data-source-info-generator.ts`) only ever iterates `dataModelConfig.tableMappings`, whose `DataSourceType` is `'InMemory' | 'Dataverse' | 'SharePoint'` — **never `'Connector'`**. A freshly added connector data source is structurally invisible to this layer.
2. The newer generated `<Connector>Service.ts`, which imports the **complete** static file `.power/schemas/appschemas/dataSourcesInfo.ts` — this one *does* contain the Connector entry.

`@microsoft/power-apps/data`'s `getClient(dataSourcesInfo)` is a lazy factory: nothing is seeded synchronously. The actual seeding happens on the first real operation call, via `PowerDataSourcesInfoProvider.getInstance(dataSourcesInfo)` — a **true singleton**:

```js
static getInstance(dataSourcesInfo) {
  if (!this.instance) { this.instance = new PowerDataSourcesInfoProvider(dataSourcesInfo); }
  return this.instance;
}
```

Whichever caller fires first across the **entire app** locks in its `dataSourcesInfo` object for the rest of the page session; every later call with a different (more complete) object is silently ignored. Since layer 1's hooks fire on every page's mount — long before a user opens whatever dialog calls the connector — the singleton always locks with the narrower, connector-less map first. `runtimeDataSourceService.js`'s `getDataSource()` then throws `PowerDataRuntimeError(DataSourceNotFound, <key>)` for the connector key, forever, for that page load.

**Fix:** merge the Connector-type entries from the full generated schema into `app-gen-sdk`'s output, so whichever caller wins the race, the singleton it seeds is already complete:

```ts
// app-gen-sdk/data/common/data-source-info-generator.ts
// (marked "autogenerated, do not edit" — edit anyway, this is the pragmatic fix
// until the scaffolding itself merges Connector-type sources on its own)
import { dataSourcesInfo as fullDataSourcesInfo } from '../../../.power/schemas/appschemas/dataSourcesInfo';

export function getDataSourcesInfo(): DataSourcesInfo {
  const dataModelConfig = getDataModelConfig(false);
  const dataSourcesInfo = convertToDataSourceInfo(dataModelConfig.tableMappings);
  for (const [key, info] of Object.entries(fullDataSourcesInfo)) {
    if (info.dataSourceType === 'Connector' && !(key in dataSourcesInfo)) {
      dataSourcesInfo[key] = info;
    }
  }
  return dataSourcesInfo;
}
```

Verify the fix by checking which layer's `getDataSourcesInfo()`/`dataSourcesInfo.ts` your app actually has before assuming this applies — the exact file names can differ by scaffold version, but the underlying singleton-race mechanism is a property of `@microsoft/power-apps/data` itself, not of any one generator.

## 3. Copilot Studio connector: `notificationUrl` is required even for synchronous use

Calling `ExecuteCopilotAsyncV2` (and likely sibling operations) without a `notificationUrl` field in the request body — even though the generated TypeScript signature doesn't mark it required — fails with:

```
400 "Invalid request body"
```
(sometimes surfacing client-side as "The response is not in a JSON format.")

**Fix:** always include a `notificationUrl`, even a placeholder, when you don't actually want async/webhook callback behavior:

```ts
await MicrosoftCopilotStudioService.ExecuteCopilotAsyncV2(agentSchemaName, {
  message: prompt,
  notificationUrl: 'https://notificationurlplaceholder',
});
```

## 4. Slow connector calls need an in-flight guard, not just a debounce

A Copilot Studio (or similarly heavy) connector call can take several seconds. A plain debounce on user input isn't enough — if the user pauses typing more than once while a call is still in flight, calls stack up and responses can arrive out of order. Track an in-flight flag and the latest input together, and re-check after each call settles:

```ts
const isFetchingRef = useRef(false);
const latestTextRef = useRef('');

async function runSearch(text: string) {
  latestTextRef.current = text;
  if (isFetchingRef.current) return; // a call is already in flight; it will re-check on completion
  isFetchingRef.current = true;
  try {
    await callConnector(text);
  } finally {
    isFetchingRef.current = false;
    if (latestTextRef.current !== text) runSearch(latestTextRef.current); // input changed meanwhile — rerun immediately
  }
}
```
